discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch — applied. Switched `honorLabels` to `{{ if hasKey .Values.serviceMonitor "honorLabels" }}` so an explicit `honorLabels: false` is now emitted instead of being swallowed by `with`. Verified with `helm template`: the default (`false`) now renders `honorLabels: false`, and `--set serviceMonitor.honorLabels=true` renders `honorLabels: true`. The other `with` blocks are strings/maps/arrays, so they are unaffected by the false-is-empty pitfall.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Verified this is not an issue: Helm deletes null-valued keys during values coalescing, before templates run, so `toYaml` never sees them. From the Helm docs (https://helm.sh/docs/chart_template_guide/values_files/, "Deleting a Default Key"): *"If you need to delete a key from the default values, you may override the value of the key to be null, in which case Helm will remove the key from the overridden values merge."*

Confirmed empirically with `helm template` using a values file setting `podSecurityContext.runAsUser: null`, `podSecurityContext.fsGroup: null`, and `securityContext.runAsUser: null` - the rendered Deployment/StatefulSet contain only `runAsNonRoot: true`; no `runAsUser: null` or `fsGroup: null` fields appear, so restricted-v2 SCC can assign its arbitrary UID as intended.
